taxonomy.vision:
# House Ontology Charter

**Status:** Draft for review, 2026-10-26. Informative, not normative: [docs/ONTOLOGY.md](../docs/ONTOLOGY.md) stays the specification. This charter states what the ontology is for, what a node and an edge are meant to model, and how a proposed change should be judged. Tooling that reasons about House's vocabulary, such as Context Studio and Claude in conversation, is given this text as its foundation.

## In one paragraph

House is a household knowledge graph that Claude reads and maintains, so that "I've got an hour for chores" becomes an ordered plan and a list of what to grab. The graph is memory and vocabulary; Claude does the interpretation. A node is a thing people name in conversation, of exactly one kind from a closed set: places (where things are and work happens), activities (kinds of work), resources (kinds of things used), items (things owned, somewhere, in some quantity), tasks, projects and tags. Concepts are kept apart from instances: a resource is never the thing on the pegboard. Every node has a short definition that says what it is plus one detail that tells it apart from its neighbours. An edge has exactly one meaning, only the kind-to-kind combinations in the schema are valid, hierarchies are acyclic, and inference along them is written down rather than assumed.

## What the ontology is for

- Filing tasks by where they happen (place) and what kind of work they are (activity), so "what's left in the garage?" and "what cleaning is due?" have answers.
- Knowing what work needs (kits of resources), what the house has and where (stock), and what is low or missing (the shopping list).
- Answering from the house's own documents: a TV's manual belongs to its model, a warranty to the unit.
- Each group (the household, a person) keeps its own vocabulary, seeded from a shared starter set of activities and then edited in place.

The split of responsibility is deliberate: the graph holds names, definitions, structure and the rules for what structure implies; Claude interprets what people say against it.

## What a node models

- A node has exactly one kind from the closed set, and optionally one subkind (a room or a storage spot among places; a tool, supply, material, appliance or furniture among resources). Adding a kind is a design change; ad hoc dimensions use tags until they earn a kind.
- **Concepts are not instances.** A resource ("Claw hammer") is a kind of thing; an item ("1 claw hammer on the garage pegboard") is a thing owned, somewhere, in some quantity. A specific make and model is a resource, a leaf under the generic kind; a unit with its own name, serial or warranty is an item. Merging the two is the most common way these models go wrong.
- **Definitions decide membership.** One or two sentences: say what or where it is, then one distinguishing detail (for a place, what it has, holds or is used for). A definition that only restates the name and the parent is too thin to tell neighbours apart.
- **Names are distinctive within the group** ("Den Bathroom", not a second "Bathroom"); the other names people use are aliases.
- **A place's parent means inside.** A room off or next to another is its sibling under the same floor, linked with `adjacent_to`, never nested in it.
- Granularity: an activity is a kind of work someone would file several tasks under; one-off phrasing belongs on the task, not in the vocabulary.

## What an edge models

- Every edge type has one meaning and runs from → to as the schema states: `is_a` runs specific → general, `part_of` runs part → whole, `requires` runs work → what it needs, `instance_of` runs instance → concept, `located_in` runs thing → place.
- Only the `(from kind, edge type, to kind)` combinations in the schema are valid; anything else is rejected.
- Hierarchies are acyclic: `is_a` is a DAG (an activity may specialise two parents), `part_of` is a tree.
- `adjacent_to` is symmetric, never transitive, and never carries tasks or stock across.
- `requires` may carry a quantity, a unit and an optional flag. Kits are inherited down `is_a`: the nearest declaration wins, and a specific resource replaces its general one.
- Inference is explicit and written down (containment rolls up, kits inherit, stock satisfies down `is_a`); nothing else is assumed.

## How to judge a proposed change

- **A defect** contradicts ONTOLOGY.md, loses information people rely on, merges a concept with an instance, or declares one thing twice (two nodes for one place, two edge types with one meaning).
- **Working as designed** covers the deliberate conventions: next-door rooms are siblings, activities are created freely and tidied later, each group owns its own copy of the vocabulary, warnings advise and never block.
- **A judgment call** is a choice with reasonable alternatives: whether a specific job deserves its own activity, where a resource sits in the `is_a` tree, which of two near-synonyms is the name and which the alias.
- **Scope of change:** a new kind, subkind, edge type, unit or inference rule is a design change (a plan, a recorded decision, a migration); new vocabulary, aliases and sharper definitions are normal edits; merges, retirements and re-parenting are maintenance. A fix should be the smallest scope that resolves the problem.

schemes.title: Vocabulary
schemes.description: The kinds people name and curate in conversation, kept per group with definitions and aliases and audited by check_vocabulary: places, activities, resources and tags.

schemes.title: Records
schemes.description: What is filed against the vocabulary: tasks, the projects that hold them, and items (stock lines and units) of resources in places.

classes.title: Place
classes.description: Where things are and where work happens: a property, building, floor, room, area or storage spot. A place's parent is the place it is inside.

attributes.title: Status
attributes.description: Active, or retired (merged away, sold, broken): kept with its history, hidden from lists.

attributes.title: Documents
attributes.description: Links to library documents, each with a role (manual, warranty, receipt, contract, other) and a label. A resource's documents are inherited by the resources below it and by its items.

attributes.title: Aliases
attributes.description: Other names people use ("family room" for Den); unique per kind within a parent, like names.

classes.title: Activity
classes.description: A kind of work, the type a task is filed under, such as Cleaning or Hang a picture. Activities specialise with is_a, broad categories above specific jobs.

attributes.title: Status
attributes.description: Active, or retired (merged away, sold, broken): kept with its history, hidden from lists.

attributes.title: Aliases
attributes.description: Other names people use ("family room" for Den); unique per kind within a parent, like names.

attributes.title: Estimate (minutes)
attributes.description: Typical duration of a task of this activity.

classes.title: Resource
classes.description: A kind of thing work uses or the house owns: a tool, supply, material, appliance or piece of furniture, down to a specific make and model. A concept, never a particular thing.

attributes.title: Status
attributes.description: Active, or retired (merged away, sold, broken): kept with its history, hidden from lists.

attributes.title: Documents
attributes.description: Links to library documents, each with a role (manual, warranty, receipt, contract, other) and a label. A resource's documents are inherited by the resources below it and by its items.

attributes.title: Aliases
attributes.description: Other names people use ("family room" for Den); unique per kind within a parent, like names.

attributes.title: Base unit
attributes.description: The unit requirements and stock are counted in; defaults to each.

attributes.title: Packs
attributes.description: Named pack sizes, each { name, quantity, unit }, e.g. box = 50 each.

attributes.title: Reorder at
attributes.description: Low-stock threshold { quantity, unit }, stored in the base unit; needs counted stock.

attributes.title: Usual buy
attributes.description: What the house usually buys on a shopping trip { quantity, unit }; empty quantity means some. A habit, never a schedule.

attributes.title: Usually every (days)
attributes.description: The usual buy's rough cadence (about weekly = 7); only shown, never scheduled.

attributes.title: Manufacturer
attributes.description: The maker of a specific make and model (a leaf resource).

attributes.title: Model
attributes.description: The exact model number; matched ignoring case, spaces and dashes.

classes.title: Item
classes.description: Something owned, somewhere, in some quantity: a stock line (how many, and where) or a unit with its own name, serial or warranty. Always an instance of exactly one resource.

attributes.title: Status
attributes.description: Active, or retired (merged away, sold, broken): kept with its history, hidden from lists.

attributes.title: Documents
attributes.description: Links to library documents, each with a role (manual, warranty, receipt, contract, other) and a label. A resource's documents are inherited by the resources below it and by its items.

attributes.title: Aliases
attributes.description: Other names people use ("family room" for Den); unique per kind within a parent, like names.

attributes.title: Item kind
attributes.description: A stock line (how many of a resource, kept in one place) or a unit (one named thing).

attributes.title: Quantity
attributes.description: A decimal number; empty means some, not counted; 0 means usually kept here, out now. Always 1 for a unit.

attributes.title: Unit
attributes.description: A unit in the resource's dimension, or one of its pack names.

attributes.title: Note
attributes.description: Free text about this line or unit.

attributes.title: Serial
attributes.description: Units only: the serial number.

attributes.title: Purchased on
attributes.description: Units only: a date, YYYY-MM-DD.

attributes.title: Installed on
attributes.description: Units only: a date, YYYY-MM-DD.

attributes.title: Warranty until
attributes.description: Units only: a date, YYYY-MM-DD.

classes.title: Task
classes.description: A piece of work to do, filed in a project, optionally of an activity and in one or more places.

attributes.title: Status
attributes.description: Open or done.

attributes.title: Notes
attributes.description: Free text about the task.

attributes.title: Estimate (minutes)
attributes.description: Overrides the activity's estimate.

attributes.title: Schedule
attributes.description: Recurrence { rule (an RFC 5545 RRULE), anchor (calendar or completion) }; empty means one-time.

attributes.title: Due
attributes.description: A calendar date, YYYY-MM-DD, in the household's time zone.

classes.title: Project
classes.description: A container of tasks, such as House Tasks or a kitchen remodel; projects nest with part_of.

attributes.title: Documents
attributes.description: Links to library documents, each with a role (manual, warranty, receipt, contract, other) and a label. A resource's documents are inherited by the resources below it and by its items.

attributes.title: Aliases
attributes.description: Other names people use ("family room" for Den); unique per kind within a parent, like names.

attributes.title: Status
attributes.description: Active or done.

classes.title: Tag
classes.description: A free-form label for a dimension that has not yet earned its own kind, attachable to any node.

attributes.title: Status
attributes.description: Active, or retired (merged away, sold, broken): kept with its history, hidden from lists.

attributes.title: Aliases
attributes.description: Other names people use ("family room" for Den); unique per kind within a parent, like names.

classes.title: Property
classes.description: A whole property, the top of a household's place tree.

classes.title: Building
classes.description: A building on a property: the house, a garage, a shed.

classes.title: Floor
classes.description: A floor or level of a building, holding its rooms.

classes.title: Room
classes.description: A room on a floor. A room off or next to another is its sibling, not inside it.

classes.title: Area
classes.description: A named area that is not a room, such as the back yard or under the stairs.

classes.title: Storage
classes.description: A storage spot inside a room: a shelf, bin, drawer or pegboard, where stock is kept.

classes.title: Tool
classes.description: A durable resource reused across jobs: a hammer, a level.

classes.title: Supply
classes.description: A resource used up by the work: picture hooks, cleaning spray, vacuum bags.

classes.title: Material
classes.description: A resource that becomes part of the work: spackle, paint.

classes.title: Appliance
classes.description: Equipment the house owns and maintains: a TV, the dishwasher, the furnace.

classes.title: Furniture
classes.description: Something owned and placed, never used up: a credenza, a bookcase.

properties.title: activity is_a activity
properties.description: Specialisation, specific to general: Vacuuming is a kind of Cleaning. A DAG; one node may have two parents.

properties.title: resource is_a resource
properties.description: Specialisation, specific to general: Vacuuming is a kind of Cleaning. A DAG; one node may have two parents.

properties.title: tag is_a tag
properties.description: Specialisation, specific to general: Vacuuming is a kind of Cleaning. A DAG; one node may have two parents.

properties.title: place part_of place
properties.description: Containment, part to whole: Closet is in Primary Bedroom; a sub-project is part of a project. A tree.

properties.title: place adjacent_to place
properties.description: Next to, off or opens onto: Den Bathroom is off the Den. Symmetric, never transitive, never implies containment.

properties.title: project part_of project
properties.description: Containment, part to whole: Closet is in Primary Bedroom; a sub-project is part of a project. A tree.

properties.title: task in_project project
properties.description: The project a task is filed in; every task has exactly one.

properties.title: task instance_of activity
properties.description: What an instance is: a task's kind of work, or an item's resource (its model when known).

properties.title: item instance_of resource
properties.description: What an instance is: a task's kind of work, or an item's resource (its model when known).

properties.title: task located_in place
properties.description: Where a task happens or where an item is kept.

properties.title: item located_in place
properties.description: Where a task happens or where an item is kept.

properties.title: activity requires resource
properties.description: What work needs: a resource, with an optional quantity, unit and optional flag. Kits inherit down is_a; the nearest declaration wins.

properties.title: task requires resource
properties.description: What work needs: a resource, with an optional quantity, unit and optional flag. Kits inherit down is_a; the nearest declaration wins.

properties.title: task depends_on task
properties.description: Must be done first: patch the hole before painting the wall. A DAG.

properties.title: place tagged tag
properties.description: An ad hoc label from any node to a tag.

properties.title: activity tagged tag
properties.description: An ad hoc label from any node to a tag.

properties.description: An ad hoc label from any node to a tag.

properties.description: An ad hoc label from any node to a tag.

properties.description: An ad hoc label from any node to a tag.

properties.description: An ad hoc label from any node to a tag.

properties.description: An ad hoc label from any node to a tag.

individuals.title: Cleaning
individuals.description: Making a space or object clean: removing dirt, dust, grime or mess.

individuals.title: Vacuuming
individuals.description: Cleaning floors, rugs, stairs or upholstery with a vacuum cleaner.

individuals.title: Dusting
individuals.description: Wiping dust off surfaces such as shelves, furniture, baseboards and fixtures.

individuals.title: Mopping
individuals.description: Washing hard floors with a mop and cleaning solution.

individuals.title: Bathroom cleaning
individuals.description: Cleaning a bathroom: toilet, sink, tub or shower, mirrors and floor.

individuals.title: Kitchen cleaning
individuals.description: Cleaning kitchen counters, appliances, sink and cabinet fronts.

individuals.title: Window cleaning
individuals.description: Washing window glass, frames and sills, inside or out.

individuals.title: Laundry
individuals.description: Washing, drying, folding and putting away clothes and linens.

individuals.title: Organizing
individuals.description: Arranging belongings so they are easy to find and put away.

individuals.title: Organize storage
individuals.description: Sorting and arranging a closet, cupboard, shelf, bin or garage so things have a place.

individuals.title: Decluttering
individuals.description: Going through belongings to donate, sell or throw away what is no longer needed.

individuals.title: Wall work
individuals.description: Jobs on interior walls and ceilings: hanging things, patching and painting.

individuals.title: Hang a picture
individuals.description: Hanging a picture, frame, mirror or artwork on a wall with suitable hardware.

individuals.title: Hang a shelf
individuals.description: Mounting a shelf or rack on a wall, anchored into studs or with wall anchors.

individuals.title: Patch a hole in the wall
individuals.description: Filling and smoothing holes or dents in drywall or plaster, ready for paint.

individuals.title: Painting
individuals.description: Painting walls, ceilings, trim or doors, including prep and cleanup.

individuals.title: Repairs
individuals.description: Fixing something in the house that is broken, leaking or not working properly.

individuals.title: Plumbing repair
individuals.description: Fixing leaks, drips, clogs or running toilets in sinks, tubs, toilets and pipes.

individuals.title: Electrical repair
individuals.description: Small electrical fixes such as replacing a switch, outlet or light fixture.

individuals.title: Furniture repair
individuals.description: Fixing wobbly, broken or damaged furniture: tightening, gluing, replacing parts.

individuals.title: Maintenance
individuals.description: Routine upkeep that keeps the house and its systems working, done before things break.

individuals.title: Replace a light bulb
individuals.description: Swapping a burnt-out bulb in a lamp or fixture for a working one.

individuals.title: Replace filters
individuals.description: Changing filters in the furnace or air conditioning, range hood, water filter or vacuum.

individuals.title: Gutter cleaning
individuals.description: Clearing leaves and debris out of gutters and downspouts so water drains away.

individuals.title: Yard work
individuals.description: Outdoor work on the lawn, garden beds, trees and paths.

individuals.title: Mowing
individuals.description: Cutting the lawn with a mower, and trimming the edges.

individuals.title: Weeding
individuals.description: Pulling or removing weeds from garden beds, lawn and paths.

individuals.title: Raking leaves
individuals.description: Raking or blowing fallen leaves and bagging or composting them.

individuals.title: Watering plants
individuals.description: Watering indoor plants, garden beds or the lawn.

individuals.title: Furniture assembly
individuals.description: Putting together flat-pack or delivered furniture from its parts.

individuals.title: Shopping
individuals.description: Buying supplies, parts or household goods needed for the house or a job.
